title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical People Operations guide for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager best practices at Redwood Inference. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, people-ops partners, and engineering managers who run teams. The guidance below balances consistency and candidate experience with speed and operational efficiency.

Key objectives:
- Reduce time-to-offer while maintaining high quality of hire.
- Provide a predictable, consistent onboarding experience that accelerates new hire productivity.
- Run fair, documented performance cycles with clear expectations and timely feedback.
- Empower managers with tools, templates, and checkpoints to support career growth and compliance.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Intro: Our hiring process is structured to be inclusive, bias-mitigating, and efficient. The standard flow below is required for roles with headcount approval; variations (e.g., contractor, referral fast-track) are documented in the People Ops intake form.

Step-by-step (owner in parentheses):
1. Requisition creation & approval (Hiring manager + People Ops): Complete the hiring intake form in Greenhouse and obtain budget/headcount approval. Include role scope, must-have skills, and proposed compensation band.
2. Recruiter brief (Recruiter): 30‑minute kickoff to align on sourcing strategy, diversity goals, and timeline.
3. Job posting & sourcing (Recruiter): Post to standard channels (LinkedIn, Lever/Greenhouse, internal mobility) and run targeted outreach.
4. Resume screen (Recruiter + Hiring manager): Reject/non-next steps within 3 business days.
5. Recruiter screen (Recruiter): 30 minutes to assess interest, compensation alignment, and core qualifications.
6. Technical/functional interview loop (Hiring manager & Panel): Standard loop includes 3 interviews: technical deep-dive, system design / architecture, and on-the-job sample or practical exercise where appropriate. Each interviewer uses the standard scorecard.
7. Collaboration / culture fit interview (Cross-functional peer): Focused on collaboration, communication, and company values alignment.
8. Hiring debrief & calibration (Hiring manager + Panel + Recruiter): Consolidate scorecards, discuss risks, and decide: proceed to offer, reject, or run follow-up interview.
9. Compensation & offer approval (Recruiter + People Ops + Finance): Confirm salary, equity, sign-on eligibility, and SLA for offer approvals is 48 hours.
10. Offer extension (Recruiter): Verbal offer followed by written offer in Greenhouse.
11. Negotiation & close (Recruiter + Hiring manager): Standard negotiation window is 5 business days. Counteroffers escalate to Head of People Ops.
12. Background & references (People Ops): Initiate background checks and reference calls once verbal acceptance is received.
13. Preboarding (Recruiter + Onboarding lead): Provide pre-boarding kit, equipment plan, and first-week agenda.

Hiring timeline targets:
- Requisition -> first phone screen: 7 business days
- Phone screen -> onsite/loop: 10 business days
- Offer decision after loop: 3 business days
- Typical total time-to-offer: 3–5 weeks depending on role level

Interview scorecard (required) — use this template for every interviewer:
- Overall recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / On hold / No hire
- Technical competence (1–5)
- Problem solving & approach (1–5)
- System design / architecture (1–5) — if applicable
- Communication & collaboration (1–5)
- Role fit & potential impact (1–5)
- Red flags / concerns (free text)
- Strengths (free text)

Standardization rules:
- Each interviewer must submit a scorecard within 24 hours of the interview.
- Hiring managers cannot be the sole approver for ICs above L6 without Executive recruiter sign-off.

2) Offer & negotiation guidance

Comp bands and approvals:
- Compensation bands are published in the People Ops Compensation matrix (linked in the People Ops hub).
- Any offer above the published midpoint requires VP-level approval and Finance notification.

Offer components to confirm in the offer email:
- Base salary, equity grant, sign-on bonus (if applicable), target bonus plan, start date, manager name, and new-hire link to benefits enrollment.

Sample offer email subject:
"Redwood Inference — Offer for [Candidate Name] (Role, Team)"

Negotiation best practices for managers:
- Focus on total comp and role level, not only base pay.
- Use precedents from recent similar offers in the last 90 days.
- Escalate exceptions early to People Ops.

3) Preboarding & Day 1 onboarding checklist

Preboarding (before start date):
- Send welcome email with first-week agenda and logistics (Recruiter).
- Confirm equipment delivery and access to Slack, email, and SSO (IT & Onboarding ops).
- Assign onboarding buddy and onboarding owner (Hiring manager).
- Complete benefits enrollment instructions and paperwork (People Ops).

Day 1 — sample agenda (Onboarding owner must customize):
- 09:00 — Welcome + HR check-in (30m)
- 09:30 — Team welcome & role overview (Hiring manager)
- 10:15 — Workspace & tools walkthrough (IT)
- 11:00 — Security & compliance briefing (Security)
- 12:00 — Team lunch (virtual/in-person)
- 13:30 — Product overview & roadmap session (Product/Eng)
- 15:00 — 30-day objectives & expectations (Manager)

30-60-90 day ramp plan (manager responsibilities):
- 0–30 days: Access, basic training, meet core team, deliver first small milestone (doc, bugfix, feature spike).
- 31–60 days: Take ownership of a medium-sized task, start contributing to team rituals, initial 1:1 rhythm established weekly.
- 61–90 days: Independently own a cross-cutting feature/initiative, present a runbook or demo, and prepare performance checkpoint.

Onboarding artifacts and required sign-offs (table):
| Artifact | Owner | Sign-off required by |
|---|---:|---|
| Equipment & SSO access | IT | Hiring manager confirmation |
| NDA & employment paperwork | People Ops | People Ops completion |
| Security training | Security | Security team confirmation |
| First 30-day objectives | Manager | New hire acknowledgement |

4) Performance and feedback cycles

Cadence and scope:
- Continuous feedback: Encourage peers and managers to give frequent feedback through Slack, 1:1s, and the performance system.
- Quarterly check-ins: Informal written check-in to capture progress, blockers, and alignment.
- Formal performance cycle: Annual review (calendar Q4) with optional mid-year calibration for promotions/comp adjustments.

Performance rubric (single-line summary to include in review):
- Impact: Measurable product or infrastructure outcomes (delivery, reliability gains, revenue impact)
- Quality: Code quality, design rigor, and error rates
- Craft: Domain expertise and ability to mentor others
- Collaboration: Cross-team influence and communication
- Growth: Learning velocity and role expansion

Ratings scale (examples):
- Exceeds expectations 
- Meets expectations 
- Needs improvement

Manager checklist for formal review:
1. Collect input: gather peer feedback, stakeholder comments, and engineering metrics (PR throughput, incident runbook contributions).
2. Complete manager narrative: strengths, development areas, recommended compensation action.
3. Calibration: Participate in org-level calibration meetings to ensure equitable outcomes.
4. Documentation & HR approval: Submit completed packet to People Ops for compensation processing.

Promotion & leveling guidance:
- Promotions require demonstrated impact above the target level for a sustained period (~6–12 months), strong manager advocacy, and cross-functional references.
- Use the Leveling rubric (linked) to justify promotion cases.
- Compensation adjustments for promotions should follow the band rules; any exception escalates to People Ops.

5) Manager responsibilities & best practices

Primary responsibilities:
- Set clear expectations and 30-60-90 plans at hire.
- Run weekly 1:1s and provide regular, documented feedback.
- Own performance calibration, compensation recommendations, and development plans.
- Ensure psychological safety and inclusion in the team.
- Track capacity and raise hiring requests early (recommended at 70% utilization).

Manager checklist (recurring):
- Weekly: 1:1s, team standup attendance, backlog review.
- Monthly: Check career development goals, update onboarding progress, sync with people-ops.
- Quarterly: Career conversations, calibration prep, promotion candidates review.

Giving feedback (structured approach):
1. Situation — describe context.
2. Behavior — describe observable behavior.
3. Impact — describe effect on product/team/customer.
4. Next steps — suggest concrete changes and follow-up timeline.

Handling low performance & PIPs:
- Document concerns early in written form and offer targeted coaching and resources.
- Typical informal improvement plan: 30 days with weekly check-ins.
- Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP): 60–90 days depending on role level, with clear objectives and measurable success criteria. People Ops must be engaged before initiating a PIP.

6) Probation, offboarding & role changes

Probation: New hires are on a 90-day probationary period. Managers must conduct a 30-day and 90-day checkpoint and document outcomes.

Offboarding checklist (owner in parentheses):
- Initiate offboarding in HRIS (People Ops).
- Revoke SSO and VPN access (IT) on last working day.
- Conduct knowledge transfer and update runbooks (Manager).
- Exit interview and benefits de-enrollment (People Ops).

Role changes / internal mobility:
- Employees may apply internally; managers should support transfer conversations and complete the internal transfer form.
- Hiring manager for the receiving team must coordinate with the current manager to ensure a smooth transition.

7) Templates, links & appendices

Included templates (available in the People Ops drive):
- Interview scorecard (Google Form)
- Offer email template
- Day 1 onboarding agenda template
- 30-60-90 plan template
- Manager performance narrative template

Common links:
- People Ops hub: /confluence/people-ops (internal)
- Compensation bands: /confluence/people-ops/compensation-matrix
- Leveling rubric: /confluence/people-ops/leveling-rubric

Appendix A — Example manager feedback note:
"On the 2026-01-10 deploy incident, you clearly documented the rollback steps and coordinated the postmortem. The runbook you authored reduced mean time to recovery by 22%. For next steps, pair with Jenna to outline monitoring alerts that can detect the root cause earlier."

Appendix B — Quick checklists (copyable)
- Hiring checklist copyable:
  - Requisition approved
  - Recruiter brief completed
  - Job posted & sourced
  - 3 interviews scheduled and scorecards assigned
  - Offer approval queued

- Day 1 manager checklist copyable:
  - Team introduction scheduled
  - First-week objectives sent
  - Onboarding buddy assigned
  - Dev environment access confirmed

Governance & change control
- People Ops owns this document and will review annually or when major policy changes occur. Managers should escalate process improvement suggestions to people-ops@redwood.ai.

If you have questions or need an exception to any item above, contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai) or your assigned recruiter.
